title: A Market From Around the World
strapline: Fruit and spices, cloth and baskets — step up to the world market stall.
intent: A world-market role-play brings foods, goods and traditions from many cultures together in busy, purposeful play.
Buying, selling and paying is real early maths — counting coins, giving change, comparing prices and quantities.
Naming and handling goods from around the world builds vocabulary and knowledge of where things come from.
Serving customers, taking turns and running a stall grows language, cooperation and social confidence.
The market honours the many cultures in the room and the wider world through the things people trade and eat.
implementation: Set up stalls with goods from many cultures — fruits, spices to smell, cloth, baskets, bread — plus a till, coins and bags.
Model the market talk: 'How much are the mangoes? Can I have three, please? Here's your change.'
Weave in maths — counting purchases, adding coins, comparing which stall has more, which costs more.
Feed in knowledge lightly — where the fruits and spices come from, how they're used, what they're called.
Invite families to suggest goods or a stall from their own culture to include.
Follow the play — some children will run the stalls, others will shop, haggle and fill their baskets.
key_questions: How much do these cost — how many coins do you need?
Which stall has more, and which has fewer?
Where do you think this fruit comes from?
What can you smell at the spice stall?
What job does the stallholder need to do next?

impact.text: Children count coins and goods, compare amounts and give change in play.
Children name and handle goods from around the world and talk about where they come from.
Children run and use the market with cooperative roles and turn-taking.
Children show respect and curiosity for goods and foods from other cultures.
Children use rich talk to buy, sell and negotiate.

enhancements: Stalls of world goods — fruits, spices to smell, cloth, baskets, breads — with a till and coins.
Shopping baskets, bags, purses and price labels to make and read.
A spice-smelling corner to explore aromas from around the world.
A family-suggested stall celebrating one culture's goods or food.
Real (empty, clean) packaging and produce from a range of cuisines.

playing_exploring: Children throw themselves into buying, selling and filling their baskets.
They handle and explore goods and smells from around the world.
active_learning: Children run a stall and keep the market going, seeing transactions through.
They work at counting coins and giving the right change.
creating_thinking: Children reason about prices, amounts and change.
They connect goods to the places and cultures they come from.
